title: Where the Empire Withdrew, 1683–1923
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Mediterranean Travels
description: Classify fourteen places of the former Ottoman Empire by the era in which they left Ottoman rule, then replay the four eras on a map to see the shape of the retreat.

learningObjectives: Classify fourteen places on a map of the former Ottoman Empire by the era in which they left Ottoman rule, with at least 10 of 14 correct on the first attempt.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Predict, then reveal (classification on a map), followed by a cumulative era replay
keyQuestions: Which regions did the empire lose first, and which last?
Which lost places became independent states, and which passed to another empire?
Why did the Arab provinces stay Ottoman until World War I?
commonMisconceptions: The Greek and Balkan lands were the last to go, because they were closest to Istanbul.
The Arab provinces broke away early.
The empire lost its lands in one collapse in 1918.
Every lost place became an independent nation at once.
assessmentOpportunities: First-attempt score on fourteen places (mastery: 10 of 14).
Compare when Rhodes and Athens left Ottoman rule and when each became Greek.
